intro: If a patient is being given a recommendation by ambulance personnel that transport to a medical facility by ambulance is not required, the crew must pause briefly to go through the non-transport checklist (below) and agree that non-transport is the right decision. If consensus is unable to be easily achieved, personnel should have a low threshold for recommending the patient is transported.
instruction: The following non-transport checklist must be completed prior to leaving the scene:
items: The patient has been fully assessed including a set of vital signs and appropriate investigations.
There are no unexplained abnormal vital signs.
Serious illness or injury has been reasonably excluded.
No red flags requiring transport to ED are present.
The patient is seen to mobilise safely (when able to normally do so), noting that if the patient is unable to mobilise there must be a minor or long-standing condition preventing this.
The patient and/or caregivers have been given a verbal and written explanation of when to seek further help or advice.
